title: Limited Query Retention and Provisioning Agreement (Template)
content:
Purpose

This template is intended for use when Redwood Inference ("Provider") agrees to provide inference services to a customer ("Controller") where the customer requires explicit contractual limits
on: (a) how long raw or derived query data is retained, (b) under what circumstances the Provider must provide copies of retained queries, and (c) the
procedures for rapid revocation or legal hold on retained queries. This doc is a working draft — aims to sit alongside the DPA as a discrete exhibit.

Key drafting notes (working):
- Keep appetite for minimal retention by default; allow customer-requested retention windows if they buy dedicated/enterprise plans.
- Explicitly carve out telemetry/metrics aggregated for platform operation (non-identifiable).
- Include a short playbook for rapid revocation and evidence collection for e-discovery requests (SLA and contact points).

Agreement template (select bracketed options as appropriate)

1. Definitions
1.1. "Query Data" means the textual and binary content of requests submitted to the Provider’s inference endpoints, including any prompts, user-supplied context, and service-generated intermediate artifacts (e.g., model logits or traces) that are stored.
1.2. "Retention Window" means the period during which Query Data is stored in a form retrievable by the Provider.
1.3. "Provisioning Event" means one of: (a) Controller’s written request for Query Data as part of a compliance exercise; (b) a lawful subpoena or court order; (c) an incident response request under Section 6.

2. Scope and Purpose of Retention
2.1. Provider shall retain Query Data only for the minimum time reasonably required to provide the Services and to comply with Controller’s expressed retention selection. Default retention for hosted plans is 24 hours unless otherwise agreed in writing.
2.2. Controller may request retention beyond default by purchasing an opt-in retention addon or by being on a Dedicated/Private plan. If Controller elects extended retention, the Parties shall document the Retention Window and any special access controls in Schedule A.

3. Access, Provisioning and Escrow-Like Delivery
3.1. Upon receipt of a Provisioning Event, Provider will: (a) verify the identity and authorization of the requestor per the procedures in Schedule B; (b) produce the requested Query Data scoped to the time range identified; and (c) deliver data in the format agreed (JSON newline-delimited, with metadata headers).
3.2. Timing and SLA: For Controller-initiated Provisioning Events (excluding legal process), Provider will acknowledge within 24 hours and deliver a first export within five (5) business days, except where production would be unduly burdensome. For emergency involuntary disclosure required by law, see Section 8.
3.3. Escrow-like custody (optional): Where Controller requires an additional guarantee of availability for e-discovery, Provider may offer an archival snapshot export to a mutually-controlled cloud bucket or a neutral escrow provider on a quarterly basis. Custody, access controls, and costs are defined in Schedule C.

4. Data Minimization, Masking and Redaction
4.1. Provider will apply non-reversible hashing or tokenization to known PII fields by default for retained Query Data where feasible, and will document transformation rules in Schedule D.
4.2. Controller and Provider will jointly maintain a redaction playbook for sensitive patterns (e.g., SSNs, financial account numbers, health identifiers). Redaction adequacy is a best-effort obligation; Controller remains responsible for providing sensitive markers where necessary.

5. Legal Hold and Rapid Revocation
5.1. Upon Controller’s issuance of a Legal Hold Notice (as per Schedule E), Provider shall suspend scheduled deletion of Query Data covered by the notice and implement expedited retention safeguards. Provider will confirm implementation within 24 hours.
5.2. Provider’s Obligations During Hold: Maintain immutable copies for the duration of the hold, limit access to a narrow role list, and record all access. Provider may charge reasonable fees for extended holds beyond 90 days, unless otherwise agreed.
5.3. Rapid Revocation: If Controller issues a Revocation Request requiring deletion of a specified subset of retained Query Data, Provider will (i) validate the scope within 48 hours, (ii) execute deletion from active and nearline stores within five (5) business days, and (iii) provide a signed attestation of deletion. Note: deletion from backups will occur per Provider’s backup retention policy and may be on a longer cadence; Provider must document backup deletion timing and provide reasonable verification steps.

6. Access Controls, Logging and Audit Evidence
6.1. Provider will restrict access to retained Query Data to authorized personnel and to system processes necessary for operation. Access must be role-based and logged.
6.2. Audit Evidence: Provider will retain access logs for a minimum period equal to the Retention Window plus 90 days. Upon Controller request, Provider will deliver redacted access logs tied to a Provisioning Event within the SLA in Section 3.2.

7. Incident Response and Notifications
7.1. If Query Data is subject to an unauthorized access incident, Provider will follow the incident response obligations in the DPA and notify Controller consistent with those timelines. Provider will include in its incident report: a description of the data exposed, the Retention Window affected, and mitigation/remediation steps.

8. Law Enforcement and Compelled Disclosure
8.1. Provider will notify Controller of any compelled disclosure (e.g., subpoena) unless legally prohibited. Provider will cooperate with Controller in attempts to limit scope and will only disclose the minimum data required by the process.

9. Liability, Indemnities and Limitations
9.1. Provider’s liability for breaches of the retention and provisioning obligations shall be governed by the DPA’s liability cap, except where gross negligence or willful misconduct is identified.

10. Termination and Data Return/Destruction
10.1. Upon termination of the Services, Provider will return or securely destroy retained Query Data per Controller’s election. Return will be in a structured format; destruction will be permanent to the extent reasonably practicable and Provider will provide an attestation of destruction.

Schedules (to be customized per engagement)
Schedule A: Retention Window and Access Roles (example values)
- Default hosted: 24 hours (raw); 30 days (metadata logs)
- Extended: 90 days / 1 year / custom on Dedicated plans
- Access roles: Platform-ops-readonly, Incident-team, Legal-evidence (min list)

Schedule B: Provisioning Authentication Flow (example)
- Controller raises a ticket to legal@redwood.ai with request ID; Provider routes to Evidence team; two-person verification; export signed and delivered to Controller S3 / secure transfer.

Schedule C: Archival Snapshot / Custody Options
- Option 1: Quarterly export to Controller-controlled S3 with server-side encryption and limited ACL
- Option 2: Neutral escrow provider (additional fees, separate custodian agreement)

Schedule D: Redaction/Masking Examples
- PII hashing: SHA-256 of normalized email addresses with salt (non-reversible)
- Caution: Non-PII transformations (e.g., entity replacement) may affect model outputs and must be tested.

Schedule E: Legal Hold Notice Template
- Required fields: Scope, Dates, Contact, Ticket ID, Sample Query Identifiers (if known)

Open items & negotiations (notes to drafter)
- Decide whether Provider will support per-query redaction by Controller via API (technical feasibility/price).
- Define backup snapshot deletion cadence more precisely for Dedicated vs Hosted customers.
- Consider a separate price schedule for long-term legal holds (> 90 days).

Revision history / contributors
- 2024-10-02 Sophie M.: initial draft and outline
- 2024-11-12 Evan S.: added provisioning SLA language and escrow options
- 2025-03-10 Priya N.: fleshed out redaction examples and legal hold attestation text

References
- See related artifacts: DPA template (confluence link above), Incident Response SLA (confluence: IR-ops-2023), and Backup/DR policy (internal doc: infra/backups).

End of template.

(This doc is intentionally conversational in parts — meant for security/legal/solutions teams to iterate before finalizing as an Exhibit to the DPA.)
